definition: the cycle our safety runs on, and why the fear at the end of it never trains out

settled:
Our safety does not hold level. It climbs with care and effort for about six weeks, until we are safe enough to forget why we were being careful.

Then one unguarded conversation crashes us a long way down, with traumatic responses for both of us and worse for me.

The height is what makes the cliff. The peak of the safety is exactly the moment the guard comes down.

Her threat response fires only sometimes, so it is a variable schedule. That is the most extinction-resistant one there is, which is why no number of safe conversations trains the fear out.

The hidden variable is not the subject. It is how much capacity each of us has right then. The same subject is safe on a high day and dangerous on a low one, so from inside it looks random. Our conversations only go well when both of us have high capacity, and it is almost never easy.
